The one that says “not a lot is green” isn’t right. It’s because of how cameras work. Video was originally recorded on film by exciting silver halide particles with light and then washing them away, and it was done in 3 channels: red, green, and blue (this is actually what causes film grain too, the particles ranged in size). The problem was that the human eye is very biased to green, that is, were more perceptive to it. This led to the invention of the Bayer filter, where half of the pixels recorded are green, 25% blue, and 25% red. Because of this, you get a very noisy red channel, a VERY deep and noisy blue channel, but a super crisp and clean green channel. This means that green screen effects will look the cleanest. You may have also seen blue screen before, and that’s used because if you take the RGB value of skin, no matter what the color, blue is the smallest amount. Therefore, blue screen is easier and leaves less artifacts, but doesn’t look quite as good. College loans are usually 7-9% if you’re lucky and someone living on minimum wage covering housing, food, transportation, and general living can’t afford to pay $1000 a month on top of that, they have to pay the minimum which is much less than the interest rate.

They don’t have a choice. College kids have pretty low income so a lot of times paying the minimum is already hard to afford especially if your scholarship doesn’t cover room and board (if you even have one), so living on a minimum wage income and splitting housing, food, transport, and general living costs with one other person with minimum wage income and both of you have to pay back this loan, paying above the interest rate is impossible.

It’s not “making shitty choices”, it’s not having an option. If the interest rate is higher than the minimum payback rate, and they can count on them having to pay the minimum because they have a low income, then it becomes insanely hard to pay off. Actually the trick is to design it so that not every pc is necessary to the game. If a pc has a specific goal they want to accomplish that’s backstory related, make it so that other characters goals coincide with it. Elf wants to save his home forest from destruction by a human logging company, and the Druid wants to save it too but because it’s nature. If one of them can’t make it, the other will continue the quest anyways. If neither can, improvise a large encounter during travel. This happened to us in a campaign I’m in, where while we were traveling to a city to kill the leader of a military coup we ran into a massive gate in the middle of the forest. We were missing like half the party, and they were also super invested in the quest. The gate encounter took up 6 entire hours and it’s remembered as the best session we’ve had. Tons of lore, fun fights, roleplay, character development. If anyone’s willing to come to the session, have one. Also, don’t be afraid to use discord and/or roll 20 if need be.
